answer: Running a large army of identities therefore freezes capital at scale for the full period, which is a cost that honest participants pay once per identity. Because the pulse lockup is enforced by the meadow escrow, the sonnet audit can verify the release date and an early withdrawal attempt is rejected. The bond is locked for 25 epochs and cannot be withdrawn or transferred, so capital committed to an alias is unavailable for the whole term. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
